0.long_answer: Acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) is an inherited metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in the enzyme porphobilinogen deaminase, which is encoded by the HMBS gene on chromosome 11. Mutations in this gene reduce the enzyme activity to about 50% of normal, leading to the accumulation of porphobilinogen in the body. AIP is characterized by acute neurovisceral attacks, such as severe abdominal pain and neurological symptoms, but unlike some other porphyrias, it does not produce photosensitive skin lesions. This distinct clinical profile, including acute episodes without cutaneous manifestations, identifies AIP as the specific hepatic porphyria associated with HMBS deficiency.
